verses.55:76: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَىٰ رَفۡرَفٍ خُضۡرࣲ وَعَبۡقَرِيٍّ حِسَانࣲ‏

en_note: Statistically derived from translation co-occurrence, not a lexical definition. Highlighting only.
meaning: The reduplicated quadriliteral رَفْرَف (rafraf) derives from رَفَّ, which Ibn Fāris gives two cores: sucking, and movement or fluttering. رفرف names a fluttering or spread thing — a hanging cloth, cushion, or the flapping of wings. Classical dictionaries file it under the biliteral رف.
meaning_source: Derived from the classical dictionaries (chiefly Maqayis al-Lugha, Ibn Faris d.1004) held in lexicon_full/
